title: Button Bounce Timeline
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A slow-motion timeline that shows how one button press on pin 20 makes many falling edges, and how a debounce window decides which edges the interrupt handler counts as presses.

educational.topic: Button debouncing and GPIO falling-edge interrupts
learningObjectives: Explain why one mechanical button press produces several falling edges and therefore several IRQ handler calls.
Trace how the test ticks_diff(now, last_press_time) > window accepts or ignores each falling edge.
Select a debounce window that is longer than the contact bounce but shorter than the gap between two real presses.
prerequisites: GPIO HIGH and LOW levels and pull-up resistors (Chapter 6)
GPIO interrupts and the IRQ falling edge trigger (Chapter 7)

controls.label: Press
controls.purpose: Simulate one press with a new random bounce pattern.

controls.label: Press twice quickly
controls.purpose: Simulate two real presses 100 ms apart.

controls.label: Reset counters
controls.purpose: Clear the timeline and set both counters to 0.

controls.label: Show code
controls.purpose: Show the button_pressed() handler with the live window value.

assumptions: Each press makes 3 to 12 bounces spread across the bounce length, then settles LOW.
Button releases are drawn as one clean rising edge.
limitations: Real releases also bounce and can add falling edges.
Time is continuous; real ticks_ms() counts whole milliseconds.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Slow-motion replay followed by live re-evaluation of the same edges as the window slider moves
keyQuestions: How many times does the interrupt handler run for one press?
Why is the second of two quick presses sometimes missed?
What two limits must a good debounce window fall between?
commonMisconceptions: One press always makes exactly one interrupt.
A longer debounce window is always safer.
The release of the button fires IRQ_FALLING.
assessmentOpportunities: Exit question: choose a working and a failing window for a 20 ms bounce and 250 ms press spacing.
Read an edge tooltip aloud using the words falling edge, window, and ignored.
Find the largest window that still counts both quick presses.
